title: Dynamic Price-Headcount Coupling: micro-buckets & runway scan (May 2026)
content:
Purpose: quick model and decision table to show how marginal price moves and small targeted hiring surges (micro-buckets of HC) interact to change runway and margin outcomes. Use this as an operational playbook for price gates during high token-velocity periods.

Summary (short):
- We simulate 3 price pivots + 4 hiring-surge levers across 6 month and 12 month horizons.
- Output metrics: net margin delta, runway months remaining, SLA risk index (inferred), and burn delta.
- Key insight: small targeted hiring swaps (contractor -> perm or pause) combined with a ~6% effective price uplift on the top 20% of high-intensity customers yields >30% runway improvement vs. global across-the-board price hikes.

Model assumptions (base case):
- Base token price (hosted API blended): $0.015 per token.
- Model mix: 65% open-quantized (low cost), 25% standard (medium), 10% large-newer (high cost).
- Monthly token volume (current): 45B tokens. Growth: 6% mo.
- Avg fully-burdened headcount cost (engineer/ops): $220,000 /yr => $18,333/mo. Customer-facing roles averaged $160,000/yr => $13,333/mo.
- Reserved GPU cost per equivalent capacity unit: $35k /month for a 4-GPU cluster slice.
- Cache/batching efficiency assumed stable at 12% token reduction in effective cost.

Micro-bucket definitions (targeted HC pools):
- Pool A (On-call / SRE stretch): 5 FTE equivalents - low replacement flexibility - high SLA impact if cut.
- Pool B (Solutions & onboarding): 8 FTE equivalents - medium churn sensitivity - high revenue linkage.
- Pool C (Platform infra & runtime): 12 FTE equivalents - long lead to replace - moderate immediate revenue linkage.
- Surge tactics: contractor freeze, delayed new grad offers, contractor-to-perm swaps, and temporary overtime for Pool A.

Pricing levers simulated:
- L0 (No change) = $0.015 / token (base).
- L1 (Micro-tilt) = +6% price only on top 20% customers by token intensity (effective blended uplift +1.2%).
- L2 (Tiered uplift) = +10% on top 20% and +3% on next 30% (blended +4.1%).
- L3 (Global uplift) = +8% globally (blended +8%).
- Elasticity assumptions: elasticity = -0.6 on top 20% (sticky), -1.1 on mid 30%, -1.6 on tail. We apply conservative churn friction for known enterprise accounts (-0.2 additional retention stickiness).

Scenarios run (representative):
- Scenario A: L0 price + no HC change (base).
- Scenario B: L1 price + pause hiring for Pools B & C (save 20 FTE months over 6 months).
- Scenario C: L2 price + convert 6 contractor FTEs to freeze + 4 perm offers delayed (saves 30 FTE months).
- Scenario D: L3 price + across-the-board 10% headcount reduction (aggressive).

Representative outputs (6-month horizon) - aggregated:
- Base (A): Net burn = $7.1M; runway = 10.2 months; margin = -18.6%
- B (micro-tilt + selective pause): Net burn = $5.2M; runway = 13.6 months; margin = -8.9%
- C (tiered uplift + moderate HC deferral): Net burn = $4.6M; runway = 15.0 months; margin = -5.2%
- D (global uplift + 10% cuts): Net burn = $3.9M; runway = 16.8 months; margin = +2.3%

Nota bene: D shows best runway but highest operational and GTM risk; customer churn projection far more uncertain and could cascade product adoption. B and C are preferred as operational levers preserve enterprise relationships.

Sensitivity matrix (selected deltas):
- Price uplift sensitivity (blended uplift only)
  - +1% uplift => runway +0.6 months
  - +3% uplift => runway +2.0 months
  - +5% uplift => runway +3.3 months
- HC savings sensitivity
  - Save 5 FTE-months => runway +0.3 months
  - Save 20 FTE-months => runway +1.4 months
  - Save 40 FTE-months => runway +2.8 months
- Token growth sensitivity (if velocity +10% mo) => runway -2.6 months vs base across all price levers

Operational risk index (qualitative overlay):
- Low: no customer-facing churn; internal hiring pause for infra-only contractors.
- Medium: selective price tilts + delays to onboarding; measured churn in high-velocity tail.
- High: global uplifts + mass HC cuts; elevated escalations and SLA penalties.

Action playbook (recommended sequence):
1) Immediate: activate L1 micro-tilt on top 20% customers behind targeted comms + begin hiring freeze for Pools B (solutions) for 60 days. (Short term impact: ~+1.0 months runway)
2) 30-day: run targeted retention packages for affected enterprise accounts to mitigate churn; monitor token delta.
3) 60-day: if usage stabilizes, roll L1 to L2 for next-tier customers while instituting contractor pause for Pool C, capturing another +1.8 months.
4) 90-day contingency: if velocity spikes >10% mo for 2 consecutive months, shift to scenario C instrumentation (tiered pricing + temporary perm-hire pause). Avoid D unless macro shock.

Quick sensitivity checks for execs (one-pagers):
- If macro + token growth >12% in quarter, prioritize capacity over price for 8 weeks and engage sales-led credit mitigations.
- If churn from L1 > 3% revenue in top 10 accounts, rollback L1 in 2 weeks and accept HC savings instead.

Open questions / data pulls needed:
- Clean top-20% customer list with token-to-margin mapping (Finance -> provide by 2026-05-18).
- Updated contractor pipeline commitments (People Ops).
- Realized price elasticity per cohort from last two price experiments (GTM+Analytics).

Appendix (quick numbers used in sheet):
- Avg revenue per token (base): $0.011 (after cost of inference).
- Variable infra cost per token (estimated): $0.0042.
- Gross margin base: 62% before HC and fixed infra.
- Monthly fixed opex (office, comms, GA): $1.1M.

Next steps: iterate with analytics to run the cohort-level churn projection for L1 and produce a 2-slide exec summary for FR on May 18.

Prepared by: Aisha Patel (finance-ops) — model file attached in linked_artifacts. Comments welcome in-sheet.
